blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. In Britain, being polite is like a national sport. Two small words do a lot of work every day: "sorry" and "excuse me".

We say "sorry" when something already happened. Maybe you bump into a person, or you make a small mistake. "Excuse me" is different. We use it to get attention, to ask a question, or to pass by people.

These small phrases keep London's busy offices, streets and Tubes calm and friendly. British people often say "sorry" even when it is not their fault. Learn these words well, and doors open fast.

items.q: When do we say "sorry", according to the text?
items.why: "We say 'sorry' when something already happened" — depois de um erro ou esbarrão.

items.q: What do we use "excuse me" for?
options: To get attention or to pass by people
items.why: "We use it to get attention, to ask a question, or to pass by people."

items.q: The text says British people say "sorry" even when…
items.why: "British people often say 'sorry' even when it is not their fault."

items.q: The text says "doors open fast". This most likely means…
options: polite words help you a lot with people
you must run in the street
items.why: Inferência: "doors open fast" é uma imagem — ser educado abre portas com as pessoas.

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: small polite words are not important
"sorry" and "excuse me" mean the same thing
"sorry" and "excuse me" are easy but very useful
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro mostra que as duas palavras são pequenas, mas fazem muito trabalho.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicar as frases educadas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, I'm Sophie. Let me help you with two little words in English. On the London Tube this morning, I saw them everywhere, and they are very easy.

A man stepped on my foot. He said "sorry" and smiled. I said "no worries". That is all. We say "sorry" after something happens — a small bump, a mistake, or a late reply. Don't worry if it is not your fault. British people say "sorry" a lot.

Then I wanted to leave the train. There were many people in front of me. I did not push them. I said "excuse me", and people moved. "Excuse me" is for before — to get attention, to ask a question, or to pass by.

Here is a good tip. If you don't hear a word, don't say "what?". Say "pardon?". It is more polite. And at work, if you send a wrong file, you can write "my apologies" in the email. That is a formal "sorry".

One last thing. The word is important, but your voice is important too. A soft, calm voice makes any phrase sound kind. Try it today.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did Sophie say when the man stepped on her foot?
items.why: "He said 'sorry' and smiled. I said 'no worries'."

items.q: What did Sophie say to leave the crowded train?
items.why: "I said 'excuse me', and people moved."

items.q: If you don't hear a word, Sophie says you should say…
items.why: "don't say 'what?'. Say 'pardon?'. It is more polite."

items.q: Why does Sophie mention "my apologies" for a wrong file at work?
options: Because it is a more formal way to say "sorry"
Because it asks people to repeat
Because it is used only on the Tube
items.why: Inferência: ela chama "my apologies" de "a formal 'sorry'" — versão mais formal para o e-mail.

items.q: What is Sophie's main point at the end?
options: Your voice and tone matter as much as the word
items.why: Inferência: "the word is important, but your voice is important too" — o tom importa tanto quanto a palavra.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Sorry, I am late for the meeting." We say sorry to…
items.why: Sorry = desculpe; usamos para pedir desculpas por algo.

items.q: Choose the correct words: "___, can I ask you a question?" (to get attention politely)
items.why: Excuse me = com licença; usamos para chamar atenção ou interromper com educação.

items.q: "I sent the wrong file. It was my mistake." A mistake is…
items.why: Mistake = erro, algo que você fez errado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I can't hear you. ___? Could you repeat that?"
items.why: Pardon? = como? — pedimos para a pessoa repetir de forma educada.

items.q: "I want to apologise for the delay." To apologise means to…
items.why: Apologise = pedir desculpas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões educadas que você ouve todos os dias no trabalho e na rua. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Thanks for waiting." "No worries!" This means…
items.why: No worries = não tem problema; resposta amigável e tranquila.

items.q: In an email: "My apologies for the late reply." This is a…
items.why: My apologies = minhas desculpas; um "sorry" mais formal, comum em e-mails.

items.q: "Sorry to bother you, but do you have a minute?" You say this to…
items.why: Sorry to bother you = desculpe incomodar; abre um pedido com educação.

items.q: "Excuse me, could I just get past?" This phrase is used to…
items.why: "Excuse me, could I just…" abre qualquer pedido educado, como passar por pessoas.

items.q: At a door, a colleague says "After you." This means…
items.why: After you = depois de você; um jeito educado de dizer "passe primeiro".
